papers.title: CFormer-PINN: A physics-informed transformer network with adaptive gating for end-point carbon prediction in BOF steelmaking
papers.abstract: Accurate end-point carbon prediction in basic oxygen furnace (BOF) steelmaking is critical. This article addresses two key challenges. Mechanism models suffer from difficult online identification of kinetic parameters. Data-driven models lack physical constraints and suffer from difficult accurate identification of critical parameters. To solve these problems, this article proposes CFormer-PINN (carbon transformer physics-informed neural network). A mechanism equation for the post-blowing stage is established and embedded as a physical constraint via physics-informed neural network. A Transformer module replaces traditional recurrent networks to enhance temporal feature extraction. A gating-based dual-branch adaptive fusion method is designed with a multi-constraint collaborative loss function. These enable automatic learning of weights between physical and data-driven branches. Experiments use 800 heats of production data from a domestic steel plant. The dataset is divided into 650 heats for training, 75 for validation, and 75 for testing. Results show that CFormer-PINN achieves hit rates of 46.67%, 82.67%, and 97.33% within ± 0.005%, ± 0.01%, and ± 0.015%, respectively. The mean absolute error is 0.00553. Compared with the pure physics model, the hit rate within ± 0.01% is improved by 17.34 percentage points. Compared with multilayer perceptron-based physics-informed neural network, the improvement is 12.71 percentage points. The proposed model significantly enhances prediction accuracy and physical interpretability for carbon content prediction in the post-blowing stage.

papers.title: When uncertainty sampling backfires: A benchmark of active learning query strategies on real image datasets
papers.abstract: Active learning promises to reduce annotation cost by letting a model choose which unlabelled examples should be labelled next, but published gains vary widely and some strategies have been reported to perform worse than random selection. This study compares six query strategies under identical conditions on three real image datasets: handwritten digits from MNIST, product photographs from Fashion-MNIST and the smaller UCI Digits collection. Starting from 20 randomly chosen labelled images, a logistic-regression classifier was retrained after each batch of queries until 1,000 images (400 for Digits) had been labelled, with five random seeds per condition. The strategies were random sampling, least-confidence, margin and entropy uncertainty sampling, k-center greedy diversity sampling, and margin sampling combined with k-means diversification of each batch. Margin sampling with batch diversification was the most label-efficient strategy on all three datasets: it reached 95% of the accuracy of a model trained on the full pool with 372, 452 and 82 labels on average, whereas random sampling needed 750 and 216 labels on MNIST and Digits and reached the target in only one of five runs on Fashion-MNIST (at 820 labels), and its area under the learning curve exceeded that of random sampling in all 15 runs. However, least-confidence and entropy sampling were worse than random sampling throughout the budget on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, and k-center greedy sampling ended 16.3 and 9.9 percentage points below random sampling on these datasets. Inspection of the images queried by each strategy explained these failures: entropy sampling repeatedly selected visually similar ambiguous digits from a few classes, whereas k-center greedy selected atypical images, whose distance to their tenth-nearest neighbour was 1.38 and 1.82 times the pool median, and over-sampled particular classes. On the small Digits dataset all strategies outperformed random sampling. The value of active learning therefore depends strongly on the strategy and the data, and margin-based sampling with batch diversity is a robust default, whereas entropy-based and purely geometric diversity sampling should be validated before use.

papers.title: A multiscale engineering design framework for integrated carbon capture and renewable hydrogen systems
papers.abstract: This study develops a multiscale engineering-design framework that links OpenFOAM-derived porous-photoreactor transport with reduced-order photoelectrochemical (PEC) hydrogen production, KOH-based carbon processing, State–Task Network (STN) scheduling, Model Predictive Control (MPC), multisite logistics, and techno-economic evaluation, so that reactor-scale transport physics informs infrastructure sizing and investment decisions. CFD simulations quantify transport enhancement, pressure loss, and species accessibility within porous photoreactor geometries, feeding a reduced-order PEC model coupled with a screen-and-refine design-optimisation procedure. Applied to Odense and Kassø using hourly solar-irradiance data, the CFD-informed design produces ∼8,585 t H2/year, €28.90 million/year profit, €444.31 million NPV, and 19.35% IRR. PEC-only is infeasible within investigated bounds, whereas electrolysis-only gives €380.55 million NPV. Neglecting the CFD transport correction raises apparent NPV to €614.53 million and cuts photoreactor area by 33.3%, showing transport fidelity affects both economic valuation and infrastructure sizing. Coordinated Odense–Kassø gives highest NPV, and ±20% solar-resource perturbations remain feasible (NPV €415.1–472.7 million). Transport fidelity, hybridisation, price-responsive dispatch, and spatial coordination affect infrastructure design and economic value, and reactor-scale improvements alone do not guarantee the greatest system-level benefit.

papers.title: Machine-Learning Mapping of Fabric Knit Parameters for Optimal Biodegradable Poly(lactic Acid) Textile Triboelectric Nanogenerators
papers.abstract: Abstract Self-powered wearable systems require energy harvesters that are mechanically compliant, comfortable, and environmentally sustainable. Here, we report a bio-based, biodegradable textile triboelectric nanogenerator fabricated from knitted poly(lactic acid) (PLA) and use machine learning to elucidate how macroscopic knit architecture influences triboelectric performance. Interlock structures were varied in gauge, stitch length, thread number, and fabric area to study combination−performance relationships. Bayesian optimization with a discrete Gaussian process regression model was employed to identify the fabrication parameters (stitch length, gauge, and fabric area) that maximized the voltage output. Gauge 8 showed the lowest response variability and the most stable behaviour during optimization. In subsequent characterization with a differential probe, the selected PLA fabric paired with PTFE film yielded VRMS = 1.11 V at 40 N and 1.5 Hz. PLA formed effective triboelectric pairs with polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), which produced the highest output, and styrene-ethylene/butylene-styrene (SEBS), which offered comparable performance and improved textile compatibility. The device was able to power an LED under high-load and high-frequency actuation, maintaining stable performance over 10,000 cycles. These results highlight knit architecture as a key design lever for sustainable, fabric-integrated triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) and demonstrate the value of small-data Bayesian optimization in wearable energy harvesting.

papers.title: Serotype‐Tailored Midstream and Downstream Operations to Advance the Manufacturing of Adeno‐Associated Viral Vectors
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Adeno‐associated viruses (AAVs) are the leading vectors for in vivo gene therapy, fueling a growing demand for scalable and robust biomanufacturing processes. Yet, the impact of cell lysis conditions on the performance of midstream and downstream unit operations across serotypes remains poorly characterized. This study presents a serotype‐resolved investigation of cell lysis and its cascading effects on AAV2, AAV5, AAV8, and AAV9 processing. A panel of lysis methods including inorganic agents, non‐ionic and ionic detergents, and mechanical disruption was evaluated using an analytical framework of at‐ and off‐line assays to quantify AAV yield, purity, and activity at each stage. Our results reveal pronounced serotype‐specific differences: cetrimonium bromide (CTAB) delivered the highest transduction output of any condition evaluated for AAV8 (2.25 × 10 9 TU/mL) at 55.0% capture step yield, while sodium deoxycholate achieved ~ 98% host cell protein (HCP) reduction for AAV9 (HCP log reduction value 1.60) and the highest functional enrichment for AAV5 (6.73‐fold) and AAV8 (5.80‐fold). AAV2 proved uniquely challenging, with CTAB enabling the highest tangential flow filtration (TFF) yield. Acid precipitation paired with high salt addition reduced aggregation and improved permeate flux for AAV5 and AAV9. TFF performance was governed by the detergents' physicochemical properties: micelle‐forming agents generated multicomponent complexes that fouled membranes in condition‐ and serotype‐specific patterns. Rheological characterization revealed that all clarified lysates converged to the viscosity of the media after filtration, supporting transferable TFF parameters. Mixed‐mode chromatography using a peptide‐functionalized resin amplified lysis‐imprinted differences, decoupling step yield from functional enrichment. Bayesian optimization of the chromatographic step improved purification outcomes: for AAV8 residual HCPs in the eluate decreased > 300‐fold, from 0.91 mg/mL to 3 μg/mL, while for AAV9 the yield rose to ~95% at residual HCP as low as 14 μg/mL, demonstrating that purity and recovery are co‐optimizable when lysis, midstream, and downstream conditions are rationally paired.

papers.title: Universal machine learning force fields for materials simulation: From model construction to complex-system applications
papers.abstract: Abstract Machine learning force fields (MLFFs) can achieve first-principles accuracy within validated chemical and configurational domains while maintaining computational efficiency comparable to classical force fields for atomistic materials simulations. Currently, MLFFs are evolving from system-specific models toward universal MLFFs. This review summarizes recent progress in universal MLFFs from data construction, model architecture, fine-tuning strategy, physical priors, and complex-system applications. We focus on three reliability bottlenecks: potential energy surface softening due to biased near-equilibrium pretraining data, catastrophic forgetting during downstream fine-tuning, and insufficient treatment of long-range electrostatics, dispersion, and polarization. Representative datasets and benchmarks are discussed together with typical universal MLFFs. We further review forgetting-aware fine-tuning strategies, physics-enhanced frameworks and polarizable long-range models, as well as representative applications in battery electrolytes, solid-state interfaces, ferroelectric phase transitions, phonons, defects and thermal transport. Finally, future directions are discussed toward multifidelity data fusion, task-oriented benchmarks, uncertainty quantification, interpretability and integrated simulation toolchains.

papers.title: Generative AI-supported problem-based learning for enhancing computational thinking and chemistry achievement in engineering chemistry
papers.abstract: The increasing adoption of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in higher education has created new opportunities to enhance active learning; however, empirical evidence regarding its integration with Problem-Based Learning (PBL) in Engineering Chemistry remains limited, particularly for simultaneously fostering Computational Thinking (CT) and chemistry achievement. This study investigates the effectiveness of integrating GenAI with PBL in an undergraduate Engineering Chemistry course within a Mechanical Engineering Education program. In the intervention, GPT-4 was embedded as an AI learning scaffold that guided students through Socratic questioning, provided formative feedback, and supported problem decomposition and analysis during collaborative PBL activities rather than supplying direct answers. Employing a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design, the study involved 68 undergraduate students (n = 34 experimental; n = 34 control) selected through cluster random sampling. Data were collected using three validated instruments: a Computational Thinking Test (CTT, 30 items, ? = .87), a Chemistry Achievement Test (CAT, 35 items, ? = .84), and a Learning Observation Sheet (LOS, 20 items, ICC = .91). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Shapiro-Wilk normality tests, Levene's homogeneity tests, independent-samples t-tests, ANCOVA, and Cohen's d effect size analysis. The results revealed significant improvements in both CT skills (t(66) = 8.47, p .001) and chemistry achievement (t(66) = 9.12, p .001) in the experimental group compared with the control group. ANCOVA controlling for pretest scores confirmed significant treatment effects for CT (F(1,65) = 127.84, p .001) and chemistry achievement (F(1,65) = 109.07, p .001), with large practical effects (Cohen's d = 2.14 and 2.06, respectively). These findings provide empirical support for integrating AI-supported scaffolding within structured PBL environments to strengthen computational thinking and conceptual understanding in Engineering Chemistry, while extending the pedagogical application of AI-enhanced constructivist learning in engineering education.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The speed control of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) is addressed in this article through an approach grounded in the model predictive control (MPC) strategy with a finite control set (FCS‐MPC). The optimization procedure of FCS‐MPC is notably simple and intuitive. As a result, FCS‐MPC finds growing application in the control of electrical drive systems. The core of the proposed strategy is a cascaded control structure, where an inner FCS‐MPC current control loop is combined with an outer velocity Sliding Mode Control (SMC) loop. Given their widespread industrial use, PMSMs frequently employ FCS‐MPC for current control. This is attributed to its fast dynamic characteristics, inherent constraint‐handling capabilities, and the possible removal of a dedicated modulator. Moreover, SMC has gained traction as a highly effective approach for PMSM velocity control, primarily because of its strong resilience to both model uncertainties and disturbances. Compared to the conventional PI cascaded control typically employed by Whirlpool in domestic appliances, the proposed approach has shown a significant enhancement in control performance and robustness.

papers.title: Holding the Room: Designing Interaction without Technology in Large Chinese University Lectures
papers.abstract: In Chinese universities, undergraduate lectures of eighty to one hundred and thirty students have become the norm. Faced with such rooms, teachers often feel that meaningful interaction is out of reach without technological support: smart response systems, live bullet-screen chat, or AI-mediated question platforms. This paper argues that the bottleneck in large lectures is design, not technology. It proposes that “interaction” in a large room should be redefined away from public speech by a few visible students and toward a ninety-second cognitive operation in which every student is engaged at the same time. Drawing on recent empirical work on active learning, retrieval practice, and large-class teaching, the paper identifies three structural constraints of the Chinese large lecture—the voice problem, the accountability problem, and the timing problem—and translates them into three reusable, no-technology interaction patterns: neighbour recount, folded-paper vote, and three-sentence exit. Holding the attention of a hundred or so students is a design task, and a smart classroom platform can support—but hardly replace—the teacher’s weekly practice of inserting three ninety-second cognitive contracts into a forty-minute lecture.

papers.abstract: Nursing education requires the safe acquisition of technical procedures. In nursing technical schools, such acquisition depends on access to and pedagogical use of mannequins, models, clinical equipment and audiovisual resources. This study examined the influence of teaching materials on the effectiveness of teaching and learning professional nursing techniques in nursing training institutes in Kinshasa. A descriptive mixed-methods and quasi-experimental study involved 1,200 students, 250 teachers and 50 inspectors or pedagogical analysts. Data were collected through questionnaires, interviews and a pre-test/post-test comparison between an experimental group receiving resource-supported teaching and a control group. Descriptive statistics, Student's t-test and thematic analysis were used. Seventy percent of inspectors reported an absence of teaching materials, and 65% of teachers considered their quantity insufficient or very insufficient. Among students, 66.7% reported that materials were available, mainly mannequins. At the post-test, the experimental group achieved a mean score of 6.10 compared with 3.46 in the control group; the difference was statistically significant (t = 5.660; p < 0.05). Teaching materials can improve academic performance and practical competence when they are available, functional and embedded in active learning. Availability alone is insufficient; teacher development, scheduled practical work and institutional monitoring are essential.

papers.title: Scenario-Based Optimization of Net Irrigation for Winter Wheat in the Huaihe Basin, China, Using AquaCrop-OSPy Constrained by Multi-Source Remote Sensing
papers.abstract: Spatial heterogeneity and sparse management observations complicate regional irrigation planning. We constrained AquaCrop-OSPy with remotely sensed canopy cover (CC) and actual evapotranspiration (ETa), together with gridded profile soil moisture (SM), using Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization. Regional simulations covered 500 m cells with at least 70% winter wheat cover in the Huaihe Basin, China. Four stage-specific irrigation thresholds were optimized to maximize incremental irrigation water productivity while maintaining at least 95% of a model-defined reference yield. Three individually calibrated historical growing seasons represented dry, normal, and wet conditions. Separate evaluation against field observations from four growing seasons yielded normalized root mean square errors (NRMSE) of 18.29% for aboveground biomass and 4.54% for grain yield; county-level yield NRMSE ranged from 12.58% to 15.88%. Using annual winter wheat fractions as area weights, mean seasonal irrigation depths over irrigated wheat area were 154.98, 119.48, and 64.09 mm, with corresponding net irrigation volumes of 5.73 × 109, 3.81 × 109, and 1.16 × 109 m3. Excluding cells that violated the SM or ETa error criterion reduced these volumes to 5.01 × 109, 3.30 × 109, and 1.06 × 109 m3 over the remaining domain. Irrigation was concentrated during the sowing-emergence and flowering-grain filling stages under dry conditions, and during the sowing-emergence and jointing-heading stages under normal and wet conditions. Mean simulated yield reached 96.67% to 97.57% of the reference yield. These model-derived estimates describe optimized net irrigation under the specified objective and yield constraint, rather than minimum irrigation requirements or independently validated schedules. Scenario differences jointly reflect climate, initial conditions, calibrated parameters, and annual spatial coverage.

papers.title: One‐Step Fabrication of Multifunctional Superhydrophobic Surfaces With Photothermal and Electromagnetic Shielding for Anti‐Icing/De‐Icing
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Ice accumulation poses significant safety hazards and economic burdens across industrial sectors. Photothermal superhydrophobic coatings provide a practical yet promising solution. However, their fabrication typically requires complex multi step processing, limiting scalable implementation. Herein, we report a one step selective laser melting (SLM) strategy to construct biomimetic rose petal papillary structures directly on Fe‐based metallic glass surfaces (RPMS), eliminating post processing requirements. This biomimetic architecture and amorphous metallic substrate synergistically generate robust photothermal effects, achieving rapid surface heating to 42.9°C under 1 sun. The hierarchical array structure establishes broadband photonic traps, enabling high absorption efficiency across the full solar spectrum. Furthermore, the resultant superhydrophobicity delays ice nucleation, whereas the photothermal effect facilitates rapid de‐icing. Electromagnetic shielding measurements indicate that RPMS achieve an average total shielding effectiveness of 39.1 dB. The combination of passive anti‐icing, active photothermal de‐icing, and electromagnetic shielding within a single surface highlights the multifunctional advantages of the proposed RPMS. This integrated design holds substantial application potential for wind energy, aerospace, and rail transportation systems, advancing the development of all weather anti‐icing/de‐icing platforms.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Hybrid Optimization Techniques for Non-Traditional Machining: A Comparative Review of Recent Advances and Applications
papers.abstract: Non-traditional machining (NTM) processes—electrical discharge machining (EDM), electrochemical machining (ECM), laser beam machining (LBM), abrasive water jet machining (AWJM), and ultrasonic machining (USM)—are indispensable for producing geometrically intricate features in hard-to-cut super alloys, ceramics, and composites. Their governing physics are stiff, coupled, and non-stationary, making first-principles real-time control prohibitively expensive. This review surveys how machine learning surrogates—multilayer perceptron’s (MLPs), Gaussian process regression (GPR), adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference systems (ANFIS), and physics-informed neural networks (PINNs)—and hybrid meta-heuristic optimizers—particle swarm optimization fused with gravitational search (PSO-GSA), and NSGA-III with reference-point decomposition—are being deployed to bridge the gap between laboratory models and shop-floor control. We present the formal governing equations for each process, compare surrogate architectures on five engineering-relevant axes, and synthesize published performance improvements across six NTM modalities in a standardized table. Critical attention is given to small-data generalization failure, the inadequacy of Ra as a surface-integrity proxy, and the architectural requirements for deploying inference on embedded FPGA/PLC controllers.

papers.title: SLAFF: Shapley Local Attribution Feature Fusion with Bayesian-Optimized Ensemble Learning for Detecting Intrusions in Renewable Energy Power Systems
papers.abstract: The incorporation of the internet into modern power systems has improved real-time communication, automation, and regulation but also heightened the risk of cyberattacks. Due to the continual generation of massive amounts of high-dimensional and heterogeneous data by these systems, it is difficult to differentiate between the many types of cyberattacks. Thus, this paper proposes a novel Shapley Local Attribution Feature Fusion (SLAFF) algorithm to select the subset of features based on Shapley values and the local attribution values. Initially, the training data are balanced using the oversampling technique. The SLAFF algorithm is implemented on the balanced dataset using only the training set to avoid data leakage. The different feature subsets are formed and trained using machine learning methods with the balanced and unbalanced datasets. The ensemble model is developed using the different ML algorithms and trained using the Bayesian optimization method. The highest accuracy is achieved by the ensemble model with 95.87% accuracy on the Kaggle Power System Intrusion dataset on 25 feature subsets and 95.36% accuracy on the Figshare Power System dataset on 40 feature subsets. Thus, implementing the proposed method will find discriminative features while preserving classification performance and offering an SLAFF method for power-system intrusion detection.

papers.title: The Role of Systemic Antifibrotic Agents on Patient and Surgical Outcomes After Joint Surgery: A Systematic Review
papers.abstract: Postoperative arthrofibrosis (PTAF) is a debilitating complication of orthopaedic surgery, causing pain, stiffness, and reduced quality of life. Antifibrotic agents (statins, angiotensin receptor blockers [ARBs], and angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors [ACEIs]) have been proposed to mitigate PTAF, yet no systematic review has evaluated all three across major orthopaedic surgeries. This review synthesizes evidence on their use for preventing PTAF after shoulder, knee, and hip surgery. PubMed, Google Scholar, and Scopus were searched for clinical studies evaluating statins, ARBs, or ACEIs for PTAF outcomes with ≥90-day follow-up. Quality was assessed using MINORS and ROBINS-I. Fourteen observational studies met (12 retrospective cohort and 2 case-control) inclusion. Most studies investigated ARBs (12 studies), with fewer studies investigating ACEIs (7) and statins (5). The mean MINORS score was 17.6, and most (10/14) had serious risk of bias. In total knee arthroplasty (TKA), three studies linked ARBs to reduced manipulation under anesthesia (MUA) or lysis of adhesions, although four found no effect on MUA, range of motion (ROM), or arthrofibrosis. ACEI results were inconsistent, with one study showing modestly reduced MUA but three others no effect; ROM findings were mixed, including one reporting worse outcomes. Statins showed no benefit, and pooled TKA/total hip arthroplasty data found no drug associations with MUA. In arthroscopic rotator-cuff repairs (ARCRs), ARBs were associated with reduced adhesive capsulitis and improved ROM inconsistently. ACEI use correlated with worse ROM and patient-reported outcomes, while statins again showed no effect. A pooled analysis of arthroscopic shoulder procedures reported no associations between ARBs or ACEIs and PTAF outcomes. Current observational data provide conflicting and insufficient support for using statins, ARBs, or ACEIs to prevent PTAF. While some studies suggest a potential benefit for ARBs in TKA and ARCR, findings are inconsistent. Higher quality studies are needed to better understand their clinical role in preventing PTAF.

papers.title: Reconstructing Pesantren Learning: Kyai Authority and Santri Agency Through Jean Piaget’s Constructivism
papers.abstract: Pesantren (Islamic boarding schools) are not merely spaces for knowledge transmission but also places where Islamic values, identities, and scholarly traditions are shaped. Amid digitalization and changing educational demands, Pesantren face the challenge of maintaining Kyai (Islamic scholar/teacher) authority while expanding Santri (students) agency. This paper aims to examine the reconstruction of Pesantren learning through Jean Piaget’s constructivist perspective, focusing on the relationship between Kyai authority and Santri agency. The study employs library research and qualitative analysis of academic literature on Pesantren, constructivism, Islamic educational authority, and learner-centered education. The study analyzes the literature to identify key concepts and their relevance to pedagogical authority, knowledge construction, and Santri participation. The findings suggest that transforming Pesantren learning does not require replacing Kyai authority but reorienting its pedagogical role toward more dialogic and reflective learning. From a Piagetian perspective, Santri are active learners who construct understanding through experience, interaction, assimilation, and accommodation. This framework provides a conceptual basis for examining traditions such as sorogan, bandongan, and Musyawarah in relation to active learning and knowledge construction. However, their constructivist potential depends on how learning is conducted and how much participation Santri are given. The study conceptually connects Piaget’s constructivism with Kyai authority and Santri agency, suggesting that pedagogical authority and active learning can complement each other while preserving adab and Islamic scholarly traditions. Thus, Pesantren transformation is better understood not as a choice between traditional authority and student agency, but as an effort to develop a complementary relationship between them

papers.title: Digital Twin-Assisted Physics-Informed Graph Neural Network Framework with Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Personalized Drug Delivery Optimization
papers.abstract: The growing demand for personalized drug delivery necessitates intelligent computational approaches that can jointly analyze molecular characteristics, biological targets, physicochemical properties, and therapeutic responses.This study presents a Digital Twin-Assisted Physics-Informed Graph Neural Network (PI-GNN) integrated with Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) to facilitate drug-target response prediction and personalized therapeutic optimization.The proposed framework was developed using 52,274 drug-target interaction records, partitioned into 36,592 training, 5,227 validation, and 10,455 testing samples.Molecular structures were transformed into graphs characterized by 23 atom-level and six bond-level features, while protein sequences were represented through 24 biological attributes.Eight physicochemical parameters-molecular weight, LogP, topological polar surface area (TPSA), hydrogen-bond donors, hydrogen-bond acceptors, rotatable bonds, ring count, and fraction Csp3-were incorporated to provide physics-informed constraints to the learning process.Experimental evaluation on the log-transformed response yielded an R² of 0.4209, RMSE of 2.2985, and MAE of 1.5695 for the test dataset.Permutation-based XAI revealed TPSA as the dominant physicochemical contributor, with its perturbation increasing RMSE by 0.1662 and decreasing R² by 0.0868, followed by molecular weight, LogP, ring count, and hydrogen-bond donors.Molecular-level interpretability was further established using GNNExplainer to identify influential atoms associated with individual predictions.Input-ablation analysis showed that suppressing physicochemical and protein information reduced R² from 0.4209 to -5.0589 and 0.3276, respectively, indicating that the trained network relied substantially on these complementary information sources.The XAI-guided digital-twin module evaluated 10,661 valid molecular candidates, with 5,756 satisfying the specified drug-like constraints.For the selected biological target context, Drug ID 1049 was identified as the highest-ranked candidate, increasing the predicted log-response from 8.5935 to 15.5521, representing an 80.98% relative improvement on the modelled log-response scale and achieving a digital-twin score of 0.8905.Overall, the findings indicate that combining graph-based molecular learning with physicochemical knowledge, model explainability, and digital-twin-driven candidate screening offers an interpretable computational strategy for prioritizing promising drug-target configurations.The framework provides a foundation for subsequent experimental validation and the development of data-driven personalized drug-delivery systems.
papers.venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

papers.title: Zn–Mg–Cu triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) gradient scaffolds fabricated by selective laser melting with enhanced mechanical, degradation, and osteogenic properties
papers.abstract: Biodegradable Zn-based scaffolds have attracted increasing attention for bone repair owing to their moderate degradation rate and favorable biological properties; however, achieving coordinated regulation of mechanical integrity, degradation behavior, and osteogenic activity remains challenging. Zn–Mg–Cu triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) gyroid scaffolds with a radial pore-size gradient were fabricated by selective laser melting (SLM) and subsequently subjected to NaOH alkali-thermal activation and polydopamine (PDA) coating. The incorporation of Mg and Cu significantly enhanced the mechanical properties of the Zn alloy through solid-solution and second-phase strengthening. Meanwhile, the TPMS gradient porous architecture improved stress distribution and provided spatially graded pathways for electrolyte transport, thereby influencing degradation behavior and ion release characteristics. NaOH alkali-thermal treatment markedly improved surface wettability, and the PDA@Zn alloy scaffolds retained a hydrophilic interface; the complete surface treatment mitigated rapid ion release during the early stage of degradation. The scaffolds exhibited favorable compressive strength, controllable degradation behavior, and enhanced cytocompatibility. ICP-MS measurements revealed distinct Zn 2+ , Mg 2+ , and Cu 2+ release profiles, while the in vitro assays demonstrated favorable cell proliferation, osteogenic differentiation, and extracellular matrix mineralization. These biological responses may be associated with the combined effects of the released ions. Overall, the fabricated scaffolds exhibited favorable mechanical properties and controlled degradation behavior, while the complete surface treatment was associated with improved cytocompatibility and osteogenic activity.

papers.title: Comparative Assessment of Primary Stability, Secondary Stability, and Marginal Bone Loss in Immediate Post-Extraction Implants: A Retrospective Study of Three Implant Macro-Geometries
papers.abstract: Background: Achieving predictable primary and secondary stability while preserving crestal bone in immediate post-extraction sockets remains technically demanding. This retrospective study compared stability progression, marginal bone loss (MBL), and early complication rates across three implant systems with distinct macro-geometries placed in fresh extraction sockets. Methods: Records of 120 immediate post-extraction implants allocated to Group A (C-Tech; n = 40), Group B (Straumann BLT; n = 40), and Group C (BTK IS+; n = 40) were reviewed. Primary stability was evaluated at implant placement (ISQ T0, Day 0), secondary stability was assessed at impression taking at 12 weeks/3 months (ISQ T1), and final stability prior to prosthetic loading was recorded at 16 weeks/4 months (ISQ T2). MBL was measured radiographically 1 year post-loading. Comparative assessments of ISQ at T1/T2 and MBL were conducted exclusively on surviving implants. Results: Overall 1-year survival rates were 100% (40/40) for Group A, 97.5% (39/40) for Group B, and 87.5% (35/40) for Group C. Group A demonstrated significantly higher ISQ values across all intervals (T0: 69.8 ± 10.6, T1: 81.5 ± 5.6, T2: 84.1 ± 4.6) relative to Group B (T0: 49.3 ± 8.6, T1: 71.3 ± 4.3, T2: 72.0 ± 4.1) and Group C (T0: 44.8 ± 8.3, T1: 64.1 ± 3.1, T2: 64.1 ± 3.1; p < 0.001). At 1 year post-loading, mean MBL was significantly lower in Group A (0.22 ± 0.38 mm) and Group B (0.29 ± 0.44 mm) compared to Group C (0.97 ± 1.25 mm; p < 0.001). Conclusions: Significant differences in initial stability, secondary stability trajectories, and 1-year marginal bone levels were observed among the implant systems evaluated in immediate post-extraction sites. Implants featuring double-lead or tapered configurations were associated with higher initial ISQ readings and enhanced crestal bone preservation.

papers.title: Biomimetic Design of Polyetheretherketone (PEEK) Implantable Medical Devices: Research Progress in Structural Biomimicry and Surface Functionalization
papers.abstract: Polyetheretherketone (PEEK) has shown broad application prospects in implantable medical devices, including orthopedic, craniofacial, spinal fusion, dental, and extravascular stent applications, owing to its elastic modulus comparable to human cortical bone, excellent mechanical properties, good biocompatibility, and radiolucency. However, the inherent bioinertness and hydrophobicity of PEEK hinder firm osseointegration with surrounding bone tissue after implantation and limit its multiple biological functions, such as antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, pro-angiogenic, and lubricating activities, thereby restricting its clinical use in complex physiological environments such as infection, post-tumor resection rehabilitation, and artificial joints. In recent years, inspired by natural bone tissue, extracellular matrix, biomineralization processes, and mussel adhesive proteins, biomimetic design strategies have been widely explored to enhance the bioactivity and mechanical adaptability of PEEK implants. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in the biomimetic design of PEEK implantable medical devices, focusing on two main aspects: structural biomimicry (porous/gradient structures, biomimetic lattices and layered architectures, and surface topographies) and surface functionalization (bioactive coatings and mineralization modification, and biomolecule/drug immobilization and controlled release). Their current applications in craniofacial reconstruction, spinal fusion, joint replacement, long-bone prostheses, dental implants, and extravascular stents are also summarized. In addition, current limitations of biomimetic design are analyzed, including coating stability, multifunctional integration, biofunctionalization of three-dimensional structures, and clinical translation. Future research should prioritize multifunctional synergy and spatiotemporal sequential regulation, smart microenvironment-responsive systems, precise fabrication of cross-scale gradient structures, and artificial intelligence-driven personalized design, thereby driving the translation of PEEK implants from passive substitutes to active next-generation high-performance medical devices capable of regulating the tissue microenvironment.

papers.title: An AI–Digital Twin Approach to Closed-Loop Risk-Aware Resource Orchestration
papers.abstract: Dynamic resource systems must respond to changing operating conditions, uncertain disturbances, and competing performance requirements. Static allocation and prediction-only strategies may fail to incorporate the risk implications of future system states into repeated resource decisions. This study develops an AI-Digital Twin approach to closed-loop risk-aware resource orchestration. The approach uses observation-based twin synchronization, a supervised multilayer perceptron for future-state prediction, an action-dependent risk operator, and a constrained utility-cost-risk objective to select resource actions over successive decision cycles. After each action is executed, the resulting system observation is used to update the twin state and inform the next decision. The approach is evaluated in a simulation comprising 120 decision cycles, four strategies, and 12 independent random seeds per strategy: static allocation, predictive allocation, risk-aware orchestration, and the proposed closed-loop strategy. Performance is assessed using utility, deployment cost, shortage, volatility, constraint violation, and composite risk. The proposed strategy achieves the highest mean utility and the lowest mean shortage, constraint violation, and composite risk among the four strategies. Relative to risk-aware orchestration, it improves utility by 2.34%, reduces shortage by 2.04%, constraint violation by 3.69%, and composite risk by 2.39%, while increasing deployment cost by 5.52%. The difference in volatility is not statistically significant. These results indicate that synchronized prediction, action-dependent risk evaluation, and feedback updating can improve selected risk-sensitive performance dimensions, although the improvement involves a measurable cost trade-off.

papers.title: Athlete-AI: a multi-modal artificial intelligence framework for personalized athlete monitoring and injury risk forecasting
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) provides opportunities for computational athlete monitoring, adaptive training analysis, and injury-risk modelling. This study presents Athlete-AI, a multimodal AI framework that integrates wearable sensor data, human motion information, pose features, and literature-derived athlete variables into a unified computational architecture. The framework combines multimodal feature fusion, reinforcement learning for adaptive training simulation, and machine-learning-based injury-risk modelling. The evaluation was conducted using publicly available benchmark datasets, including PAMAP2, Human3.6 M, and Microsoft COCO, together with literature-derived parameters used to construct simulated athlete profiles, workload, fatigue, recovery, and injury-risk scenarios. The framework was evaluated through computational experiments and simulation-based athlete-monitoring scenarios to examine multimodal integration, injury-risk classification, and adaptive training behaviour. Repeated-run evaluation across five random seeds, probability-calibration analysis, component ablation, comparison with multimodal fusion baselines, and a leakage-controlled analysis of the dependence on label-defining variables were also performed. When the workload, fatigue, recovery, and biomechanical-risk variables used to define the simulated labels were removed from the predictors, the F1-score decreased from 86.6 to 72.8%. Negative-control analyses showed that the benchmark-derived features-only model produced performance comparable to the shuffled-label control. The results demonstrate the computational feasibility of integrating heterogeneous athlete data and evaluating adaptive training and injury-risk modelling within a unified simulation environment. The reported performance values represent preliminary computational results and do not constitute real-world, clinical, or prospective athlete validation. Therefore, the proposed framework should be regarded as a computational research framework that requires validation with longitudinal data from real athletes before practical or clinical deployment.

papers.title: Annealing response and microstructural evolution of LPBF NiCoCr-based medium-entropy alloys with different interstitial contents
papers.abstract: Two NiCoCr-based medium-entropy alloys with different carbon and nitrogen interstitial contents were fabricated by laser powder bed fusion (LPBF). Alloy-specific processing parameters were optimized through a combined assessment of porosity, relative density, surface morphology, and surface roughness, and the selected samples were subsequently annealed over a range of temperatures. X-ray diffraction confirmed that both alloys retained a single-phase FCC structure under the investigated conditions, while differences in peak positions indicated distinct lattice responses. Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) revealed contrasting microstructural evolution during annealing. The lower-interstitial alloy underwent heterogeneous recrystallization accompanied by partial strain relaxation, grain refinement, and extensive annealing twinning. In comparison, the higher-interstitial alloy showed more limited recrystallization and pronounced strain localization, reflected in increased kernel average misorientation and apparent geometrically necessary dislocation density. The hardness and microstructural results indicate distinct annealing and strengthening responses in the two alloys. The higher interstitial content of the second alloy is associated with more spatially localized lattice curvature and more limited recrystallization. This study links the contrasting annealing responses of LPBF-processed NiCoCr-based alloys to their EBSD-resolved recrystallization, twinning, and strain-localization behavior, providing new insight into the relationship between composition, microstructural evolution, and mechanical response.

papers.abstract: Single-pulse laser drilling is a highly productive method for the perforation of metal foils. Conventional pulse shapes, such as rectangular or ramped profiles, however, provide only limited degrees of freedom to adapt the temporal energy deposition to a given target hole geometry. Consequently, their ability to produce precise holes with defined inlet and outlet diameters remains limited. To overcome this limitation, temporal shaping of microsecond pulses was applied to the single-pulse drilling of 200 µ m thick stainless steel foils using an acousto-optically modulated continuous-wave laser. The resulting pulses consist of three consecutive segments, each with individually adjustable power and duration, enabling the required control to tailor the energy deposition to the desired hole geometry. Bayesian optimization was employed as a global optimization strategy to navigate the six-dimensional parameter space of pulse shapes, aiming to optimize geometric accuracy, reproducibility, and pulse-energy requirements with minimal experimental effort. In fewer than 100 experimental iterations, optimized pulse shapes were identified, resulting in holes with diameters in the double-digit micrometer range and standard deviations below 0.7 µ m at pulse energies of less than 10 mJ. A comparative analysis confirmed that these three-segment pulses outperform rectangular pulses in geometric accuracy, reproducibility, and energy efficiency, reducing the required pulse energy by up to 28%.

papers.title: Reducing boundary conditions for the Thomas–Fermi equation using a hybrid q-deformation and neural network method
papers.abstract: This study introduces a hybrid \(q\) -calculus and artificial neural network framework for the Thomas–Fermi equation of free positive ions. Its contribution is a construction in which \(q\) -deformation combines the terminal derivative and terminal-value conditions, representing three classical boundary conditions by two constraints in the deformed problem. A boundary-compatible trial solution embeds the transformed constraints, allowing training to focus on the \(q\) -differential residual. For fixed \(q<1\) , the result is a deformed approximation with a classical limit as \(q\rightarrow 1\) . Experiments across nine ionization degrees and five seeds compared the \(q\) -ANN with a benchmark, a soft-constrained PINN, and an undeformed hard-constrained classical ANN. The \(q\) -ANN produced lower RMSE than the PINN in 42 of 45 matched runs and a lower median RMSE ( \(0.004127\) versus \(0.015044\) ), although two outlying outcomes caused mean RMSE to favor the PINN and paired tests did not establish a difference. Against the hard-constrained classical ANN, the \(q\) -ANN produced lower RMSE in 44 of 45 comparisons, indicating that the observed performance is not attributable solely to exact constraint embedding. The pointwise \(q\) -ANN was approximately \(102\) times slower than the vectorized PINN. The framework provides a new boundary-transformation strategy while retaining initialization sensitivity and computational cost as limitations.

papers.title: Accelerated Discovery of Earth‐Abundant Oxygen Evolution Catalysts Through Surface‐Informed Active Learning
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of efficient electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains a challenge in alkaline water electrolysis. Discovering optimal compositions for complex multi‐element electrocatalysts is time‐intensive and resource‐consuming due to the vast compositional space. Here, we propose a hybrid computational strategy that integrates active learning (AL)‐assisted screening with density functional theory (DFT) calculations to accelerate the development of multielement alloy electrocatalysts. Our approach employs 15 cycles of active learning, with 20 NiCoFe (NCF) surface configurations evaluated per cycle, totaling 300 DFT calculations. To minimize computational cost, we utilized scaling relationships and calculated only *O and *OH adsorption energies, while the AL featurization incorporated surface configuration information. This methodology filtered the compositional space of Ni x Co y Fe 100‐x‐y alloys and identified the optimal composition of Ni 55 Co 10 Fe 35 . Experimental validation demonstrated that the optimized NCF exhibits accelerated OER kinetics and practical activity, as evidenced by a low Tafel slope of 43.07 mV dec −1 while maintaining 98.68% of its initial performance over 24 h at 10 mA cm −2 . This study demonstrates the effectiveness of the hybrid AL‐DFT strategy for resource‐efficient composition screening within the NiCoFe ternary alloy system and highlights its potential for application to other multicomponent catalyst systems following appropriate system‐specific model development and validation.

papers.title: An AI‐Driven Framework for Directed Self‐Assembly Toward Design‐Technology Co‐Optimization
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Directed self‐assembly (DSA) provides a promising route for sub‐10‐nm patterning, but its integration into design‐technology co‐optimization (DTCO) remains limited by the difficulty of translating self‐assembly process constraints into manufacturable layout solutions. Here, an artificial‐intelligence‐driven closed‐loop simulation framework for DSA is presented to convert experimentally constrained DSA process knowledge into a process‐constrained design‐space map for DSA‐aware layout decomposition. The framework integrates a three‐dimensional Ohta‐Kawasaki model with Bayesian optimization and convolutional neural network screening, enabling automated model calibration using experimental racetrack‐template data without manual tuning. It efficiently identifies optimal model parameters, achieving a mean simulation‐experiment error below 1.5 nm while maintaining morphological consistency. In addition, four multimodal large language models are further evaluated for DSA morphology screening and are shown to adapt to new image modalities and defect criteria without additional task‐specific fine‐tuning, relying solely on text‐based rules and few‐shot examples. The calibrated model enables target‐constrained inverse design of experimentally validated template windows, translating DSA constraints into a manufacturable solution‐space map for layout decomposition. Its extension to peanut‐shaped templates without additional parameter calibration further supports DSA‐aware layout decomposition and DTCO. Overall, this work establishes an intelligent closed‐loop workflow linking experiment, simulation, and design, providing a practical route toward DTCO.

papers.abstract: This work presents a model predictive control (MPC) approach for optimizing the powertrain system efficiency of a fuel cell electric heavy-duty vehicle. The MPC determines the power split between the high-voltage traction battery and the fuel cell system so that the power demand of the drive cycle is met, while a second objective extends the lifetime of the fuel cell stack by including stack degradation in the cost function. Based on driving profile information, the controller adjusts the fuel cell power trajectory within a specified prediction horizon such that a target state of charge of the traction battery is reached at the end of the time-discrete horizon, fuel consumption is minimized, and excessive degradation is avoided. The control variables are computed from discrete-time models of the fuel cell, the truck, and the battery. The resulting non-linear optimization problem is solved with the open-source software package acados, integrated into MATLAB Simulink to achieve real-time capability. The MPC is implemented and tested in a model-in-the-loop environment, and its real-time execution is verified on a dSPACE MicroAutoBox III rapid control prototyping unit. On the Vehicle Energy Consumption Calculation Tool (VECTO) Long Haul cycle, hydrogen consumption is reduced by 6.5%, while membrane thinning and the loss of electrochemically active surface area are reduced by 6.1% and 2.3%, respectively, compared with a rule-based strategy.

papers.abstract: In district heating systems, the large-scale deployment of room temperature collectors has accumulated massive amounts of terminal data, but these data mostly remain at the level of viewing and statistical analysis and have not been effectively connected to real-time control of district heating substations. As a direct reflection of thermal comfort, room temperature can be incorporated into predictive control of district heating substations, which can promote the transition of heating control from lagging compensation to proactive prediction. To address three engineering bottlenecks, namely, the lack of solar radiation information, significant differences in user thermal characteristics, and the accumulation of prediction errors, this paper proposes a rolling room temperature prediction method that integrates CatBoost solar radiation prediction, canonical variate analysis (CVA) subspace identification, and adaptive Kalman filtering. Based on representative users selected by clustering, a model predictive control framework with an alternating iterative solution strategy is constructed to directly serve the closed-loop control of district heating substations. The method relies only on conventional weather forecasts and existing data collected by the heating system, without additional hardware costs. Taking a residential community in Luoyang as an example, there were 490 valid users on the prediction day of 16 December 2024. Using data from the 15 days prior to the prediction day for training and hourly rolling prediction, the root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) for all users were 0.203 °C and 0.146 °C, respectively, and the RMSE under six typical weather conditions remained within 0.21 °C. Online computation only involves low-dimensional matrix operations, and the computational burden is small, demonstrating the potential for deployment on existing controllers of district heating substations and good engineering deployability.

papers.title: Association of S2 Alar–Iliac Versus S1-Only Fixation with Spinopelvic Mobility and Acetabular Component Orientation in Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Standing–Sitting EOS Study
papers.abstract: Background: S2 alar–iliac (S2AI) fixation crosses the sacroiliac joint, unlike fixation terminating at S1, and may be associated with reduced spinopelvic mobility in patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty (THA). We compared spinopelvic mobility, femoropelvic reorientation, acetabular component orientation, and hip-specific function between S2AI and S1-only fixation. Methods: This retrospective comparative cohort study included 60 patients undergoing THA after adult spinal fusion with S2AI (n = 30) or S1-only (n = 30) fixation. Standing and sitting EOS imaging at 1 year assessed changes in sacral slope (ΔSS) and pelvic–femoral angle (ΔPFA). Immediate postoperative CT measured static acetabular component orientation. Hip-specific function was assessed using the Hip Disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (HOOS). Multivariable regression evaluated associations with ΔSS and HOOS. Results: Spinopelvic stiffness (ΔSS < 10°) was more frequent with S2AI fixation (66.7% vs. 13.3%; p < 0.001). Compared with S1-only fixation, S2AI was associated with lower ΔSS (7.7 ± 4.8° vs. 18.1 ± 7.0°; p < 0.001) and greater ΔPFA (68.8 ± 11.7° vs. 58.7 ± 10.8°; p = 0.001). Static cup orientation was similar. One-year HOOS was lower with S2AI fixation (79 [68–86] vs. 86 [72–92]; p = 0.01), although ΔHOOS did not differ significantly (p = 0.07). After adjustment, S2AI fixation remained associated with lower ΔSS (β = −7.67; p < 0.001), while greater ΔSS was associated with higher HOOS (β = 3.42 per 5°; p = 0.003). Conclusions: S2AI fixation was associated with reduced spinopelvic mobility and greater femoropelvic reorientation despite similar static cup orientation. Residual confounding by spinal construct complexity precludes causal inference.

papers.title: Nanoparticle- and MSC-reinforced thermosensitive chitosan hydrogel for controlled antibiotic release and bone regeneration.
papers.abstract: Critical-sized bone defects pose major challenges in orthopedic tissue engineering due to their limited self-repair capacity and high risk of infection. To address these issues, we developed an injectable, thermoresponsive, and biodegradable chitosan (CS)-based hydrogel reinforced with mesoporous zinc-silicate (mZS) nanoparticles and platelet-derived microparticles (PMPs). The mZS nanoparticles, characterized by a rod-like zinc core encapsulated in a mesoporous silica sheath, exhibited a hydrodynamic diameter of 1423.45 ± 222.43 d.nm and a zeta potential of -24.03 ± 0.90 mV. Incorporation of β-glycerophosphate and increasing concentrations of mZS reduced gelation time (5-10 min) and improved hydrogel porosity, mechanical integrity, and surface roughness-supporting cell adhesion and proliferation. The mZS/CS hydrogels demonstrated sustained antibiotic release, potent antibacterial activity, and high cytocompatibility with the murine embryonic fibroblast cell line (C3H10T1/2). PMPs enriched the matrix with osteoinductive growth factors, thereby promoting the osteogenic differentiation of C3H10T1/2 cells without the need for external inducers. In vivo, the mZS/CS + PMP + C3H10T1/2 construct significantly accelerated bone regeneration in a rat tibial defect model, achieving bone formation within 21 days, as confirmed by radiography, Alizarin Red staining, histology and Micro-CT. The hydrogel's dual antibiotic-loading capacity (mZS pores and CS matrix) provided localized infection control, reducing inflammation and enhancing wound healing, as observed in an infected rat model. This multifunctional platform integrates bone mineralization, probable osteoinduction, antimicrobial defense, and tissue support, making it a strong candidate for bone repair, cartilage regeneration, and 3D bioprinting applications. Additionally, it shows promise in treating osteoporosis and reducing the need for systemic antibiotics post-surgery.

papers.title: Powder-based additive manufacturing of functionally graded materials: Delivery systems, gradient control, and computational modeling of powder spreading
papers.abstract: Powder-based additive manufacturing (AM) of functionally graded materials (FGMs) enables unprecedented spatial control of the composition and microstructure of multifunctional components. This review critically examines powder delivery systems, gradient-control techniques, and computational modeling approaches essential for FGM fabrication. The major AM platforms: laser powder bed fusion, directed energy deposition, wire arc additive manufacturing, and electron beam powder bed fusion, are systematically compared for gradient resolution, scalability, and defect propensity. Multi-material powder delivery systems, including multi-hopper feeders, vibratory mechanisms, and real-time blending architectures, are evaluated for gradient fidelity and segregation control. Critical process parameters, including, laser power modulation, scanning strategy, and thermal management are analyzed across platforms, revealing persistent challenges in interfacial bonding and defect formation at dissimilar material boundaries. Metallurgical mechanisms at compositional interfaces — solidification mode transitions, solute redistribution, and brittle intermetallic phase formation — are identified as direct causal drivers of interfacial cracking and delamination, mechanistically distinct from process parameter effects. The emerging potential of high-entropy and medium-entropy alloy systems as FGM base materials is discussed alongside the challenges of thermodynamic database completeness and gradient path planning in high-dimensional composition spaces. Computational frameworks employing discrete element method simulations coupled with computational fluid dynamics, and machine learning approaches, are assessed for predicting powder spreading behavior and gradient formation dynamics. Significant gaps persist in synchronized simulation–experiment pipelines, standardized qualification protocols for spatially varying properties, FGM-specific training datasets, and robust multi-material handling with adaptive feedback. Strategic research priorities spanning data infrastructure, interface-aware alloy design, surrogate modeling, closed-loop process control, and qualification framework development define the critical path towards industrially deployable FGM components.

papers.title: Mechanics-constrained Cosserat-rod digital twin for defect-aware continuous-tow composite deposition
papers.abstract: Tow-steered automated fiber placement (AFP) enables tailored laminates, but curvature and compaction can generate bending, shear, contact concentration, and deposition mismatch before inspection. In this study, we develop a Cosserat-rod reduced mechanics layer that maps programmed paths to residual-balanced deposited states and exports objective kinematics, energy, dissipation, contact response, and defect-tendency indicators. Under identical geometry, elasticity, loading, restraints, and unilateral roller contact, three states are compared with independently assembled Q4 and 43,065-DOF Hex8 models; maximum discrepancies in centerline deformation, integrated reaction, and peak of the width-averaged pressure are 0.58%, 9.69%, and 6.57%, respectively. A corrected 320-case Latin-hypercube set and a 32-case severe set all satisfy the dual convergence criterion. At N = 48 , a process/geometry surrogate reverses severe-case order ( ρ = − 0.904 ) , whereas a Cosserat-mechanics surrogate retains ρ = 0.990 and identifies all 11 high-risk cases. In a separate fixed-geometry process counterfactual, mechanics-based features recover the top-risk ordering ρ = 0.918 but underpredict all four high-risk thresholds, demonstrating why surrogate selections require nonlinear reevaluation. An unseen process candidate is reevaluated, with an absolute risk discrepancy of 2.27 × 1 0 − 4 ; prewarmed surrogate screening is 4.72 × 1 0 4 times faster than Cosserat-rod reevaluation. The evidence supports mechanics-constrained triage, not calibrated defect prediction or AFP qualification. Absolute thresholds require machine-specific experiments or calibrated high-fidelity process FE.

papers.title: Review of Insulation Ageing and Lifecycle Management for Oil‐Immersed Power Equipment: From Conventional Testing Analysis to Artificial Intelligence Method
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Oil‐immersed power equipment is a critical component for energy transmission and secure operation of modern power grids. The ageing of oil–paper insulation under combined electrical, thermal and mechanical stresses directly affects equipment lifetime and system reliability. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the ageing behaviour and full‐lifecycle management technologies of oil–paper insulation in oil‐immersed power equipment. First, the structural characteristics of oil–paper insulation and its microscopic ageing mechanisms under multi‐stress conditions are analysed. Subsequently, lifetime calculation models under electrical, thermal, and electro–thermal–mechanical coupled stresses, together with their recent application progress, are systematically summarised. Ageing condition assessment and remaining useful life prediction methods based on characteristic parameter testing and multiphysics techniques are then reviewed, followed by an overview of recent advances in ageing‐state visualisation and dynamic evolution analysis. Finally, this paper discusses artificial intelligence‐oriented intelligent operation and maintenance (O&M) systems, digital twin (DT) modelling and knowledge graph applications. Based on the review, this paper further discusses future research directions, including lifetime degradation mechanisms and dynamic prediction of oil–paper insulation under extreme operating conditions, collaborative O&M management of equipment clusters, DT‐driven proactive safety protection and full‐lifecycle O&M technologies for environmentally friendly oil‐immersed equipment. This review aims to provide a systematic theoretical basis and technical reference for full‐lifecycle management, risk early warning, and the safe and reliable operation of oil‐immersed power equipment.

papers.title: Calibrated but not safe: Conformal prediction intervals for turbofan remaining useful life near end of life and under operating shift
papers.abstract: Machine learning models that predict the remaining useful life (RUL) of aircraft engines are increasingly paired with conformal prediction, which converts point predictions into intervals with a guaranteed average coverage. In a safety-critical maintenance setting, however, an average guarantee is not sufficient: what matters is whether the interval is reliable and informative for engines that are close to failure, and whether it remains valid when the fleet differs from the data used for calibration. This study evaluates five interval methods built on ridge regression, random forest, gradient boosting and multilayer-perceptron predictors using the NASA C-MAPSS turbofan benchmark (FD001–FD004, 707 test engines), with repeated engine-level calibration splits. Coverage, width and the rate at which the interval overestimated the true RUL were measured overall and for engines with a true RUL of 30 cycles or less. Global split conformal prediction met the nominal 90% coverage on average (89–92%) and covered almost every engine near failure, but with intervals about 44 cycles wide, which is uninformative when only 30 cycles remain; it also undercovered engines with 61–90 cycles of remaining life (68–76%). Calibrating separately within bands of predicted RUL (Mondrian conformal prediction) halved the width near failure for tree ensembles (from 43.7 to 20.7 cycles for gradient boosting, p = 3 × 10−8) while keeping near-failure coverage at 96.5–97.8%, but failed for ridge regression (77%). Uncalibrated quantile regression overestimated the remaining life of 20% of near-failure engines, and conformalised quantile regression restored average coverage, but its near-failure coverage fell as low as 80% and its near-failure intervals averaged over 90 cycles. When models calibrated on FD001 were applied to engines with an additional fault mode (FD003), near-failure coverage collapsed to 37–50%, and 95% of all miscoverage under shift was overestimation of remaining life, the unsafe direction. Conformal guarantees are therefore marginal and conditional on exchangeability; prognostic intervals should be evaluated near end of life and under realistic shift before they are used for maintenance decisions.

papers.title: Strategi Pembelajaran IPAS yang Efektif dalam Meningkatkan Fokus Belajar Siswa: Perspektif Guru di MIN 1 Bantul
papers.abstract: The teaching of Natural Sciences and Social Sciences (IPAS) plays a crucial role in helping students understand various natural and social phenomena in their surroundings. In the learning process, students’ focus is a key aspect because it can influence their ability to understand the material, follow learning activities, and participate actively. However, since every student has different characteristics, interests, and abilities, teachers need to select appropriate and engaging teaching methods. The use of varied, student-centered methods, supported by learning media, can create a more active learning atmosphere and help maintain students’ focus throughout the learning process. Therefore, it is important to examine teachers’ perceptions of effective teaching methods, as teachers play a direct role in planning and implementing classroom learning activities. This study aims to analyze teachers’ perceptions of effective IPAS teaching methods for improving students’ focus at MIN 1 Bantul. This study employs a descriptive quantitative approach, with data collected via a Likert-scale questionnaire distributed to 12 IPAS teachers. The results indicate that Problem-Based Learning and Project-Based Learning are viewed as effective in enhancing students’ focus, participation, and engagement.

summary_zh.method: 采用描述性定量方法，向12名教师发放李克特量表问卷。
summary_zh.result: 教师认为问题式与项目式学习有助于提升学生专注度与参与度。
summary_zh.validation: 基于小样本问卷的描述性统计，无实验或数值验证。

summary_en.motivation: The study examines how teachers perceive effective IPAS instructional methods for sustaining students' classroom focus.
summary_en.method: A descriptive quantitative design was used, administering a Likert-scale questionnaire to twelve IPAS teachers.
summary_en.result: Problem-based and project-based learning were rated as effective for improving student focus, participation, and engagement.
summary_en.validation: Validation relies on descriptive statistics from a small teacher questionnaire, with no experimental or numerical verification.
